title: Data Subject Erasure Across Data 360 Lake and Unified Profiles

steps.prompt: A customer submits a GDPR Right to Erasure request. Records exist in source CRM, Data 360 DLOs, unified DMOs, and derived insights. What must the architect ensure for complete compliance?

options.label: Execute a governed Data Subject Rights / Forget Me request in Data 360 so erasure propagates across lake objects, unified profiles, and derived insights — coordinated with source-system deletion
options.rationale: Data 360 retains historical lake and unified layers independently of CRM deletes. A formal data subject request is required to purge or restrict processing across DLOs, DMOs, and derived artifacts while source systems handle their own copies.

options.label: Delete the Contact in core CRM and assume Data 360 will drop the profile on the next connector sync
options.rationale: Connector syncs do not automatically cryptographically erase historical lake snapshots and unified graphs. Relying on CRM delete alone leaves residual PII in Data 360.

options.label: Rename the Contact to "Deleted User" in the CRM UI and leave lake objects untouched
options.rationale: Cosmetic field edits leave PII in underlying lakehouse and insight layers, failing GDPR audit requirements.
